ingredient_conflicts.warning_message: Combining retinoids with BHA (Salicylic Acid) can cause severe dryness, peeling, and compromise the skin barrier. Use them on alternate nights.
Layering pure Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) with strong chemical exfoliants like Salicylic Acid can significantly alter formula pH levels, leading to severe redness and irritation.
Both are low-pH acids. Layering them simultaneously overloads the skin barrier, frequently resulting in stinging, localized peeling, and irritation.
Using high concentrations of Niacinamide and pure Ascorbic Acid simultaneously can occasionally cause short-term facial flushing in hyper-sensitive skin profiles.
Simultaneous use increases cell turnover too aggressively, causing inflammation and moisture barrier breakdown. Apply on separate evenings.
Combining a retinoid with an alpha-hydroxy acid significantly increases skin sensitivity to external factors. Alternate your nightly applications.
Benzoyl Peroxide is a strong oxidizing agent that can rapidly degrade Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid), rendering the Vitamin C entirely useless.
Unless specifically encapsulated, Benzoyl Peroxide can deactivate retinoid molecules while heavily compounding skin dryness and flaking.
Pure Vitamin C can break down the structure of delicate copper peptides, neutralizing the anti-aging benefits of both ingredients.
